title: LC-MT362-ManagedProjectForestAndQualifiedIdentity
clause: Define the canonical SurrealDB managed-project forest and project-qualified work-packet and microtask identity model.

scope.summary: GOAL: Implement typed SCHEMAFULL SurrealDB records and relations for a Handshake-managed project forest. A managed project node has a stable project_id, project_kind of root_project, subproject, task or prototype, optional parent relation, ownership/access scope and lifecycle metadata. Each node owns its canonical taskboard, work packets and microtasks through Locus. Workspaces, worktrees, sessions and VMs bind to a project as execution contexts but never substitute for project identity. WP and MT identifiers are project-qualified so repeated labels such as WP-1 or MT-001 cannot collide across the forest. Cross-project relations are explicit records; no ancestry is inferred from filesystem paths, product modules or display nesting.
forbidden_paths: Any SQLite/PostgreSQL schema, authority, adapter or fallback
Globally unique bare WP/MT labels as record identity
Filesystem paths or workspace ids as project identity
Implicit managed-project parentage from CKC/Tailor or another product-module hierarchy
acceptance_criteria: SCHEMAFULL SurrealDB definitions represent project nodes, allowed project kinds, parent/child relations, lifecycle state and project-owned taskboard/WP/MT relations with validated identifiers.
Canonical WP and MT keys include project_id and prevent collisions when two managed projects use the same human-readable WP or MT label.
Parent relations reject self-parenting, duplicate edges, cycles, missing parents and cross-account or unauthorized AccessSpace ancestry.
Workspace, worktree, VM and session bindings can move or be recreated without changing the managed project, WP or MT identity.
Product-module relations, including CKC as parent module of future Tailor, remain separate from managed-project forest relations unless an authorized operator creates an explicit project edge.
proof_targets: Real embedded SurrealDB schema and relation tests
Collision tests using repeated WP/MT labels in sibling projects
Cycle and denied-parent negative tests under authenticated record users
Restart proof showing project identities survive replacement of every execution context

surfaces: Managed-project tree identity badges and execution-context bindings
argus_targets: Repeated WP/MT labels shown with unambiguous project context
Workspace binding separated from project identity

enforcement_boundaries: ResourceBroker authorizes every forest traversal and identity lookup.
All privacy proof uses authenticated record users rather than root credentials.
same_project_private_resource_cases: Users in the same project but outside a private AccessSpace cannot resolve protected WP/MT identities or context bindings.
cross_account_negative_cases: Cross-account users cannot discover or attach to project nodes, parents, children, WPs, MTs or execution contexts.
derived_resource_non_widening_cases: Project-tree and identity-label projections cannot widen access beyond canonical project and AccessSpace permissions.
revocation_and_context_switch_cases: AccessSpace revocation or project-context switch invalidates prior forest traversal and identity-resolution results.
metadata_side_channel_cases: Denied parents and siblings do not leak names, counts, kinds, existence or repeated-id collision information.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Record project creation, parent change, context binding and rejected identity mutations with project-qualified correlation.
Expose orphan, cycle, ambiguous identity and stale execution-context binding checks.
Record DEFERRED-with-reason if forest-health watchers are unavailable at implementation time; never silently skip.

risk_if_missed: Bare identifiers and conflated hierarchies can attach work, permissions or automation to the wrong project and make recovery ambiguous.

risks: An unauthorized child reveals a hidden parent.
A workspace deletion destroys project identity.
A product-module hierarchy silently creates project ancestry.
minimum_controls: Composite record identities and uniqueness tests.
Record-user permission tests on every traversal.
Separate binding records for execution contexts.

research_provenance.source: MT-361 stable-main audit and approved 2026-08-27 managed-project framing; official SurrealDB record-id, relation, schema and permission documentation.
research_provenance.selected_approach: SCHEMAFULL project records with explicit graph relations, composite project-qualified work identities and separate execution-context bindings.
rejected_options: Module hierarchy reused as project hierarchy
